name: Sunita Paul

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Sunita Paul is a Kolkata-based writer and publisher associated with AABS Publishing House and Reader’s Choice magazine. Alongside her publishing and editorial work, she writes poetry and fiction. Her books include the poetry collection “Inked with Love” and the short-story collection “Surprising Strokes: Sometimes … Somewhere …”, both discussed in a literary profile by PAN-Writers Caravan.

“Make-up” begins with the vocabulary and practical steps of cosmetics before turning towards the social judgments those gestures can conceal. Its rhyming lines first follow foundation, mascara and perfume, then confront a double demand: women are encouraged to accept ageing while being shamed for its visible signs. The closing invitation to take pride in scars and flaws leaves room for adornment as a choice, even as the poem questions the pressure to wear a mask.
